title: Criterion checks name a state, never a test count
context: The replacement documentation criterion was inserted with a check reading "npm test still exits 0 at 818 of 818". Three sampled runs on clean main at 4458ba76 returned 814, 814, 814, all exit 0. A run inside the fix/close-releases-pointer worktree returned 818, which is main plus exactly the four cases in the new test/spawn/close.test.ts. Registration is static: 784 top-level test calls plus loops over frozen constant arrays and three unconditional subtests, with no environment probe, platform check or directory-listing census registering anything. So 818 is wrong on main twice over, being both a pinned count and a different tree's count. The project's own testing rule already forbids pinned counts as change-detectors wearing a census costume.
options: rewrite the check to name 814, the measured baseline on main
rewrite the check to name a state, zero failures, with no count at all
leave the count and accept it will need editing on every test addition
outcome: The check names a state and carries no number. Naming 814 would be correct today and wrong on the next test addition, which is exactly the change-detector the testing rule prohibits; a criterion check exists to decide whether the criterion is true, and a count decides only whether the suite changed size. The criterion is amended by striking it and inserting a replacement, because amend_criteria carries a new check only on an insert and a rewrite would leave the bad check attached. Recorded separately from the shipping work because it corrects my own error in composing the earlier criterion, not any lead's work.
